title: BJP Cites Fox News Report to Accuse Congress of Links to Global Protest Network
excerpt: The BJP used a Fox News Digital investigation into a network of 101 activist groups to allege Congress is part of an 'anarchy and regime change plot,' pointing to an April 2025 meeting between Sonia and Rahul Gandhi and Progressive International. Congress had not responded to the charges when the reports were published.
body:
• The BJP on Thursday cited a Fox News Digital investigation to allege that Congress is part of a coordinated global protest network spanning France, Spain, Albania and India.
  • BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia pointed to an April 10, 2025 meeting at 10 Janpath between Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and a Progressive International delegation — a meeting Congress itself had posted about on social media.
  • The Fox News report, titled 'Global Chaos Inc grows to 101 groups,' describes a network of activist organisations amplifying protest movements across nine countries.
  • Congress had not immediately responded to the BJP's charges in the reports published on Thursday. The allegations are the BJP's characterisation of the report; the report itself does not establish that Congress coordinated any protest.

The Bharatiya Janata Party on Thursday accused the Congress of being part of an "anarchy and regime change plot," citing a Fox News Digital investigation that it said linked unrest in France and protests in India to a common activist ecosystem.

Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia alleged that Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi met representatives of Progressive International at 10 Janpath on April 10, 2025, displaying a photograph he said showed the meeting. "This Progressive International organisation describes itself as a transnational anti-capitalist organisation. According to the report I showed, the unrest and vandalism of historical monuments in France, the incidents in Spain, what is happening in India, and the events in Albania are all linked to Progressive International," Bhatia claimed, according to 7Globe's account of the press conference.

The Report Behind the Charge

The Fox News Digital investigation, titled "Global Chaos Inc grows to 101 groups," maps what it calls a "red-green" network of 101 activist and advocacy organisations across nine countries, and argues that overlapping groups amplify protest narratives in several countries at once. The Indian protests at issue are demonstrations demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2113181984512241686

BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari, posting on X, demanded Congress answer whether it coordinated with Progressive International during the protests and what messaging passed between them. He also questioned a social media post by Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut about protests in Albania, another country named in the report.

"Wherever there is an elected government, they want to overthrow it. They want to destroy constitutional institutions such as the Supreme Court and Parliament, as well as historical buildings."

— Gaurav Bhatia, BJP national spokesperson

What Is Established and What Is Alleged

The meeting itself is documented: Congress's own social media post recorded the April 2025 meeting between its leaders and the Progressive International delegation. What the BJP has not publicly produced is evidence that the meeting involved coordinating protests in India, or that Congress took direction from the organisation. The Fox News report is an investigation by a partisan US outlet into activist networks; it is not a court finding or an official inquiry, and Progressive International is a public coalition of left-wing parties, unions and movements whose briefings and delegations are conducted openly.

There was no immediate reaction from Congress to the BJP's charge in the reports published on Thursday, including The News Front's account, which noted the party had yet to respond. Bhatia's language — calling Rahul Gandhi a "gaddar," or traitor — signals the BJP intends to keep the charge in its campaign against the opposition's election-commission protests. Whether Congress answers the specific questions about the meeting, and whether any evidence beyond the meeting itself emerges, will decide whether this remains a press-conference row or becomes a substantive political fight.

nri_angle: The row is over how foreign activist networks are portrayed in Indian politics — a framing diaspora readers will see echoed in overseas coverage of Indian protests.
